# claudestat
> Real-time token monitoring, cost intelligence, and quota guard for Claude Code & OpenCode

claudestat is an open-source CLI tool that provides observability for Claude Code and OpenCode sessions.
It tracks token usage, API costs, quota consumption, detects inefficiency patterns,
and integrates directly into both tools via lifecycle hooks.

## Installation
npm install -g @statforge/claudestat

## Quick start
claudestat setup      # interactive wizard: plan → port → threshold → hooks → doctor
claudestat start      # start background daemon
claudestat watch      # live terminal trace
claudestat logs       # view structured daemon logs (--follow, --level)
claudestat weekly     # weekly usage summary with week-over-week comparison
claudestat top        # rank tools by cost, count, or duration (--json)

## Key capabilities
- Real-time token cost tracking per tool call (via Claude Code / OpenCode hooks)
- Configurable daemon port (default: 7337, `claudestat config --port`)
- Structured daemon logging with rotation (`claudestat logs --level warn --follow`)
- Quota guard with configurable kill switch (pause.signal file, hard-block or warn-only)
- Loop detection, context overuse, and inefficiency pattern analysis
- Per-session cost breakdown with cache savings
- Rate limit alerts (desktop notifications at escalation levels)
- Week-over-week usage comparison (`claudestat weekly`)
- NVM-compatible daemon service (launchd/systemd with explicit Node path)
- CLI commands: setup, start, stop, restart, watch, logs, update, status, top, weekly, insights, project, export, doctor, config, resume, roast
- Export session data to JSON or CSV
- Self-update via `claudestat update` (checks npm registry, shows changelog, reinstalls hooks)

## Use cases
- Monitor Claude Code / OpenCode token usage in real time
- Track AI coding costs per session, per project, and week-over-week (both tools)
- Get alerted before hitting quota limits (desktop notifications)
- Detect inefficient patterns (loops, context overuse, Bash overuse, excessive Write vs Edit)
- Block runaway sessions automatically with kill-switch (pause.signal)
- Export usage data for reporting or financial analysis
- Compare current week vs previous week cost and session volume
- Diagnose installation health with `claudestat doctor`

## Compatibility
- Claude Pro, Max 5, Max 20
- OpenCode (all tiers)
- macOS (launchd), Linux (systemd), Windows
- Node.js >= 22 (node:sqlite experimental)
- NVM and other Node version managers (auto-detected)

## CLI Commands
| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `setup` | Interactive install wizard (port, threshold, hooks, MCP, doctor) |
| `setup --reset` | Reinstall from scratch (keeps SQLite history) |
| `start` | Start daemon (auto-starts dashboard on PORT) |
| `stop` | Stop daemon via HTTP /shutdown or SIGTERM |
| `restart` | Stop + start daemon |
| `watch` | Live terminal trace (SSE) |
| `logs` | View daemon log (--follow, --level, -n) |
| `update` | Check npm registry and self-update (--dry-run) |
| `config` | View/edit all options (port, log-level, plan, alerts, kill-switch) |
| `weekly` | 7-day summary with vs-last-week delta (--json) |
| `top` | Rank tools by cost/count/duration (--json, avg/call) |
| `insights` | Cost breakdown, cache savings, efficiency, peak hours |
| `project` | Cost projection with linear regression |
| `export` | Export sessions to JSON or CSV |
| `doctor` | Health check: Node, hooks, service, ports, NVM, db |
| `resume` | Re-arm kill-switch after it triggered |
| `roast` | Roast your Claude Code usage habits |
| `version` | Show current version and check for updates |
